title: Sanjiv Goenka's RPSG Group Buys Land Near Old Trafford to Build Cricket Training Hub for Global Franchise Network
excerpt: The Indian conglomerate has signed a multi-million-pound deal with Lancashire to develop a high-performance centre that will serve its IPL, Hundred, and SA20 franchises year-round.
body:
• RPSG Group has signed a multi-million-pound deal with Lancashire County Cricket Club to acquire 2.5 acres of land behind Old Trafford Cricket Ground in Manchester.
  • The site — a former B&Q retail store — will be developed into a high-performance training centre with indoor nets, a gym, outdoor training areas, and sports science facilities.
  • The centre will serve as a shared hub for RPSG's three franchise teams: Lucknow Super Giants (IPL), Manchester Super Giants (The Hundred), and Durban Super Giants (SA20).
  • The investment comes weeks after RPSG secured a 70% stake in the Manchester franchise for £80 million.

Sanjiv Goenka's RPSG Group is planting a permanent flag in English cricket. The Indian conglomerate has signed a multi-million-pound agreement with Lancashire County Cricket Club to acquire a 2.5-acre parcel of land behind Old Trafford Cricket Ground, where it plans to build a state-of-the-art training facility for its growing global franchise network.

The land, which was previously home to a B&Q retail store, had attracted interest from housing developers with planning permission for around 600 properties. RPSG fended off those bids, according to The Times, to secure the site for cricket.

A Shared Training Hub Across Three Continents

The facility will include indoor practice nets, a fully equipped gymnasium, outdoor training areas, and dedicated sports science and medical units. Once completed, it is expected to function as a year-round training base not just for the Manchester Super Giants — RPSG's franchise in the ECB-run Hundred — but also for the Lucknow Super Giants in the IPL and Durban's Super Giants in South Africa's SA20 league.

International and touring teams playing Test matches and ODIs at Old Trafford will also have access, according to a joint statement from RPSG and Lancashire.

"We could have chosen to do this in India but we chose to invest in Manchester and Old Trafford because we really see the potential there. Manchester has a tremendous sporting culture and Old Trafford stadium is amazing."

— Dr Sanjiv Goenka, RPSG Group Chairman

Deepening the India-England Cricket Bridge

The investment follows RPSG's acquisition of a 70 percent stake in the Manchester Super Giants. The group initially purchased 49 percent of the franchise directly from the ECB during last year's team auction, then bought an additional 21 percent stake from Lancashire for £80 million. Lancashire retains the remaining 30 percent.

Manchester Super Giants have started the 2026 Hundred season strongly, sitting at the top of the men's table with two wins from two matches. The franchise's on-field performance has coincided with Goenka's off-field push to build long-term infrastructure rather than treating the investment as a short-term play.

Goenka told The Times that the project is intended to rival Lord's Nursery Ground as a premier training facility, though the 2.5-acre footprint is significantly larger. The existing Lancashire indoor centre will be overhauled as part of the redevelopment.

Indian Capital Reshaping Global Cricket

RPSG's Old Trafford investment is the latest example of Indian business groups reshaping cricket infrastructure worldwide. Indian owners now hold majority or significant stakes in franchise leagues across England, South Africa, the Caribbean, and the United States, in addition to the IPL. The pattern is shifting from simple team ownership to long-term capital commitments in training facilities, academies, and ground development.

For the Indian diaspora in the UK — particularly the sizable community in Greater Manchester — the project offers a tangible connection between Indian sporting investment and local cricket development. Lancashire's junior and women's programmes are also expected to benefit from the upgraded facilities.

What's Next

Construction timelines have not been disclosed, but the project signals that RPSG views its Manchester investment as a multi-decade commitment. With Lucknow, Manchester, and Durban all under one umbrella, the centre could become a model for how Indian-owned franchise groups build shared global infrastructure in cricket.
